summary: Visit note form leaves a saved note behind when an image upload is rejected, and saving again creates a duplicate
description:
If the server rejects one of the images in a visit note, the note and its diagnoses are already saved, but the form stays open as if nothing was saved. Pressing Save and close again creates a second visit note.
Steps to reproduce
Open a patient with an active visit and start a visit note. Add a diagnosis and some note text.

Click Add image and pick a file the server will reject. A text file renamed to .png works: it passes the dialog and the server refuses it for its content type.

Click Save and close.

Actual behaviour
A red toast says "Error saving visit note: The file content type text/plain is not allowed". The form stays open with the title "Add visit note" and everything the user typed. A visit note encounter with the text and diagnosis already exists on the server. Clicking Save and close again creates a second encounter with the same text and diagnosis. Reproduced on a local stack: one rejected upload, two notes, zero images.
Expected behaviour
Either the note is treated as saved and the user is told which images did not upload, or a retry updates the note that already exists. In no case should a second note be created.
Investigation
onSubmit in visit-notes-form.component.tsx is a promise chain: create or update the encounter, then delete and recreate diagnoses, then upload each image with createAttachment. The catch handler only shows the toast. Nothing rolls back, and the form still believes it is creating because isEditing is derived from the launch props and never changes after the encounter is created. The second submit posts a new encounter.
Any server-side rejection the dialog doesn't catch first leads here: a content type mismatch, a size limit lower than the dialog's (O3-5988), a denied file name, or an image that fails to decode.
Proposed fix
Two reasonable shapes:
After the encounter is created, switch the form to editing that encounter, so a retry updates it and only re-sends the failed images.

On a partial failure, close the workspace as saved and show a warning naming the images that didn't upload, so the user adds them again from the note.

The first keeps the user's context, the second is simpler. Either way the reproduction above becomes the regression test.
Found while working on O3-5986, which links uploaded images to the note's encounter and makes the half-saved state easier to notice. Related: O3-5987, O3-5988.
